record_audits.database_subject: Novel antibacterial activity of beta(2)-microglobulin in human amniotic fluid.
record_audits.database_measure: Discovery: isolated from human amniotic fluid (2012 ref) as well as human broncho-alveolar-lavage (BAL) fluid (2020 ref). Sequence analysis: APD calcualted: molecular formula: C528H805N135O158S3; mol. wt: 11701.176; molar extinction coefficient: 20165; GRAVY= -0.74; Wimley-White whole-residue hydrophobicity of the peptide, 25.07 kcal/mol. Activity: Active against S. aureus ATCC25923, L. monocytogenes ATCC19115, S. epidermidis KCTC1917, E. coli ATCC25922, P. vulgaris KCTC2433 (MIC 0.3-2.4 uM). Antimicrobial conditions: it is more active against L. monocytogenes at acidic conditions pH 5.5 and below, characteristic of infection and inflammation. No activity at pH 6 or above ( Holch et al., 2020). Molecular form: It is in its non-aggregated form at pH 7 and shows fibril formation at pH 4.5 (Amyloid AMPs?). Structure: You can rotate, zoom, and view the crystal structure 1B1I here in the PDB. Updated 2/2014; 3/2023.
